transcript:
Header: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Lina Cho (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (HelioPay Head of AI), Marcus Lee (HelioPay Platform), Priya Narang (Data Eng), Tom Reynolds (Helio SRE)

Summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modelling. Goal is to define success criteria (latency/throughput/quality), gather traffic samples, pick benchmark scenarios, and agree on timeline for SE-led benchmark runs. Discussed QPS, concurrency, token distributions, burst patterns, and network/VPC constraints.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:07] Aisha: hi this is Aisha, I run the AI team at HelioPay, we want to evaluate Redwood for a realtime chat assistant and some batch reconciliation tasks
[00:13] Marcus: Marcus here, platform, I'll own infra side and feeding you logs and traffic
[00:17] Priya: Priya, data eng, will anonymize and export the token samples
[00:20] Tom: Tom SRE, network questions mostly
[00:23] Samira: great, Miguel from our SE team is here to dig into throughput and sizing
[00:28] Miguel: hi everyone, excited to dig in, little housekeeping — we'll focus on three scenarios: 1) realtime chat (low latency, moderate tokens), 2) high-throughput batch e2e (embeddings / rerank), 3) peak bursts from marketing campaigns

[02:00] Samira: can you give us top-level goals for the POC? what's success look like?
[02:05] Aisha: primary is P95 latency under 300ms for the chat flows at our expected concurrency, secondary is cost per 1M tokens below our current baseline, and third is security/compliance checks (SOC2, KMS) pass for private deployment options

[04:10] Marcus: current infra — we run a mix of services on AWS, we have K8s clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, traffic is routed through an API gateway. Peak qps for the chat endpoints is about 220 qps sustained for 10 minutes during business hours, p95 latency target we want to keep low, and concurrency per instance we estimate about 80 connections during peaks

[05:45] Miguel: ok good — can you also share token distributions? average input tokens per request, and output tokens expected?
[05:52] Priya: yes, the typical chat prompt is 80–150 input tokens and responses average 60 tokens, but for some multi-turn reconciliation flows outputs can be 400–800 tokens. We will extract histogram samples and share

[07:10] Samira: perfect, that helps frame our sizing. For the benchmark we usually model qps, concurrency, and token length distribution to pick GPU types and batch sizes. We'll propose both hosted and dedicated options — dedicated gives more predictable throughput for sustained 200+ qps loads

[08:20] Aisha: quick question — what happens if we need VPC or on-prem? our security team pushes hard on private control plane and KMS integration
[08:28] Lina: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS/HSM; we'll include private checklist. The SOC2 docs and audit logs are standard asks — we'll send the security deck after the call

[09:40] Tom: network wise, we need to understand e2e RTT and TLS termination points; do you need open inbound ports for the test?
[09:47] Miguel: we generally ask customers to whitelist a small IP range for staging, and for private deployments we can work via a VPC endpoint. We'll document exact network requirements in the checklist

[11:10] Samira: let's talk numbers — Marcus said 220 qps peak; do you expect burst multipliers?
[11:18] Marcus: yes campaign bursts can hit 2–3x baseline for short windows — so spikes to ~600 qps for 3–5 minutes aren't unheard of

[12:30] Miguel: good to know. For benchmarking we typically run tests at baseline, sustained peak (220 qps), and a burst scenario 600 qps for short windows. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and token throughput (tokens/sec) and also track cost estimates using our Optimize toolkit

[14:00] Priya: when you say tokens/sec do you measure both input + output tokens? our average whole-request token count is about 200 when you include system/context

[14:09] Miguel: yes we measure total tokens per call (input+output) since that affects decoder time and KV cache usage. For models with long output tokens (400–800) we test separate flows since they stress memory/kvcache and change batching behavior

[16:00] Samira: what about concurrency per GPU? how many concurrent requests can you safely multiplex?
[16:08] Miguel: depends on model size and quantization. For a 7B quantized model on an A10G-equivalent profile we see optimal concurrency of about 12–16 effective concurrent decodes with batching; for 13B it drops to 6–8. We'll produce a table after we see token histograms

[17:40] Aisha: are you recommending model quantization or different model family for performance vs quality tradeoff?
[17:46] Miguel: we recommend doing a small eval. Redwood Optimize will suggest quant/precision profile. Often 4-bit quantized models with a light quality check give big cost wins with negligible quality loss for chat; for long-form reconciliation we might keep fp16 variants

[19:30] Marcus: how do you handle KV cache across multi-turn dialogs? we have long histories up to 20 turns
[19:36] Miguel: we expose KV cache behavior and smart prefix caching. In practice we keep the last N tokens on the cache and use prefix match caching to avoid recomputing repeated system prompts. That reduces effective tokens and latency for multi-turn sessions

[21:00] Samira: ok timeline — we propose: Samira sends benchmark spreadsheet today, customer delivers token samples by 2026-03-23, SE runs initial sizing and shares instance suggestions by 2026-03-25, first end-to-end benchmark week of 2026-03-30 with Marcus and Tom on call

[22:15] Aisha: sounds good; also we need a clear success criteria doc — p95 <300ms for chat at 220 qps, cost target 15% better than current spending, and no blocked security items for Private deployment

[24:00] Miguel: we'll include those in the POC success doc. For benchmarking we'll produce CSV outputs: latencies, tokens/sec, cost per million tokens approximations, and fail rates. We'll also run regression checks for quality with a small eval set you provide

[25:30] Priya: what about cold-starts and cache warmup? our traffic has diurnal patterns and cold pods do affect latency

[25:38] Miguel: we always test for cold-start churn; we'll run an autoscaling policy simulation — a cold-start profile will be included in results. Dedicated pools reduce cold starts since instances are pre-warmed

[27:00] Tom: from SRE side, we care about graceful degradation — if capacity is exhausted can you fallback to a cheaper model or rate limit?

[27:12] Samira: Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant, and rate limiting per tenant. We'll demo the rollouts/fallback UI in the demo phase

[29:00] Aisha: any ask from us for the benchmark environment?
[29:05] Miguel: please provide: 1) anonymized traffic samples with token histograms and a few representative long responses, 2) a list of endpoints/paths and auth flow for staging, and 3) expected concurrency profiles during business hours

[30:30] Marcus: we'll prepare logs export — question about embedding workloads: we have nightly embeddings at 10k docs per hour, how do you size for that?

[30:38] Miguel: embeddings are typically batchable; we provide batch job configs and suggest GPU types depending on model. We'll size embeddings runs separately — they don't need low latency but throughput matters. We'll recommend a batching/parallelism config

[33:00] Samira: ok, risks and blockers?
[33:05] Tom: main risk is network egress and peering rules; also procurement for dedicated capacity might take time if legal review of SOC2/KMS docs isn't rapid

[34:20] Lina: we'll fast-track security docs and offer a standard questionnaire response. For procurement we'll provide a POC MSA template and a temporary evaluation agreement

[36:00] Aisha: curious about metrics — will Redwood provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards?

[36:08] Miguel: yes token-level cost and latency breakdowns are in the Console; we can turn on per-route tracing and export CSVs for your finance team

[38:00] Priya: when you run benchmarks, do you include network latency from our region? we have users primarily in eu-west-1 so region matters

[38:08] Miguel: we'll run the SE benchmark from us-west and eu-west variants if you want; we can also run a test from your staging VPC to measure e2e RTTs

[40:00] Samira: example outputs we'll produce: throughput vs latency curves, cost per 1M tokens for each config, recommended pool sizes and autoscale policies, and a POC success checklist

[41:30] Aisha: if the POC shows we can't meet p95 target with hosted, would Redwood recommend dedicated or private single-tenant?

[41:38] Miguel: yes typically we recommend dedicated capacity for predictable low p95 under sustained high qps. Private on-prem is an option for strict compliance but increases lead time. We'll quantify tradeoffs in the benchmark report

[43:00] Marcus: any demo or artifact links we should expect from you after this call?

[43:07] Samira: I'll send the benchmark sheet, Miguel will send a sizing template, and Lina will share security docs and the POC MSA. Links will be posted to the shared drive — watch for email from samira@redwood.ai

[45:00] Miguel: note on measurement — we'll log p50/p95/p99, token/sec, decode GPU utilization, and queue times. If you have telemetry we can ingest traces to correlate stack traces with latency spikes

[46:30] Priya: one more: evaluation for quality — we'll pick a small set of 200 prompts to check for regressions across model variants

[46:38] Miguel: perfect; please include that set in the sample upload

[48:00] Aisha: timeline recap?
[48:05] Samira: Samira: send benchmark sheet today (done), Helio to upload samples by 2026-03-23, Miguel to produce sizing by 2026-03-25, formal benchmark week of 2026-03-30. We'll aim to have a decision readout within 2 weeks after the benchmark

[50:00] Tom: ok we'll coordinate internal approvals for IP whitelisting and procurement

[50:30] Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up with next steps and calendar invites for the benchmark sessions
[50:40] Aisha: thanks everyone
[50:43] Miguel: thanks

Notes: occasional transcription errors observed (Redwood was transcribed as Redwod in places by auto-transcript), speaker labels occasionally generic during crosstalk. Shared artifacts referenced: benchmark spreadsheet (link posted), security deck (to be shared), POC MSA template (to be shared).

End of transcript.
